standards.title: Auditing Standard No. (3): Terms of Audit Engagement
standards.issued_date: 1997-06 (Accounting and Auditing Standards Board meeting No. (13), 10-11 Safar 1418 A.H., corresponding to 15-16 June 1997 A.D. — Adoption of the Standard section, unnumbered)
standards.effective_date: 1999-01-01 (financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1419 A.H. or 1 January 1999 A.D. — Effective Date section, unnumbered)
linked_standards: Financial Accounting Standard No. (1): General Presentation and Disclosure in the Financial Statements of Islamic Banks and Financial Institutions
standards.applicability: Applies to auditors appointed to audit the financial statements of Islamic financial institutions that conduct business in conformity with Shari'a Rules and Principles (para 1); also applicable to related services, though separate letters may be appropriate where other services such as tax, accounting, or management advisory services are also provided (para 3); extends to consideration of components (subsidiary, branch, or division) of a parent Islamic financial institution when the same auditor is appointed (para 18).
term_names: Auditing Standard for Islamic Financial Institutions (ASIFI)
Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI)
standards.structure: Introduction (paras 1-4); Audit Engagement Letters (paras 5-11) — Basic contents of the engagement letter (para 6), Objective of the audit of the financial statements (para 7), Management's responsibility for the financial statements (paras 8-10), Management's representation (para 11); Scope of an Audit (para 12); Form of Reports (paras 13-14); Fees (para 15); Agreement of the Terms of Engagement (para 16); Other Matters (paras 17-18) — Audit of components (para 18); Recurring Audits (paras 19-20); Acceptance of a Change in Engagement (paras 21-28); Effective Date (unnumbered); Adoption of the Standard (unnumbered); Appendix (A): Example of an Audit Engagement Letter; Appendix (B): Example of an Audit Re-Engagement Letter.
key_points: Purpose of ASIFI No. 3 is to establish standards and provide guidance on the appointment of an auditor to audit the financial statements of a financial institution conducting business in conformity with Shari'a Rules and Principles (para 1).
Two main points covered: agreeing the terms of engagement with the client, and the auditor's response to a client request to change to an engagement providing a lower level of assurance (para 1).
The auditor and the client should agree on the terms of the engagement, recorded in an audit engagement letter or other suitable form of contract (para 2).

The standard assists in preparing engagement letters for audits of Islamic financial institutions' financial statements and is also applicable to related services; separate letters may be appropriate when tax, accounting, or management advisory services are also provided (para 3).
Even where audit objectives, scope, and auditor responsibilities are established by law, engagement letters may still be informative for clients (para 4).
The auditor should send an engagement letter, preferably before commencement of the engagement, to help avoid misunderstandings (para 5).
The engagement letter documents the auditor's acceptance of appointment, the objectives and scope of the audit, the extent of the auditor's responsibilities, and the form of any reports (para 6).

Audit objective: to enable the auditor to opine whether financial statements give a "true and fair view" in accordance with fatwas, rulings and guidelines of the Shari'a supervisory board, AAOIFI accounting standards, national accounting standards/practices, and relevant legislation and regulations (para 7).

Financial statements are the responsibility of management, including maintaining an effective internal control system, properly recording transactions, safeguarding assets, and overall true and fair presentation (para 8).

The audit report should state that the financial statements and the institution's undertaking to operate per Shari'a Rules and Principles are management's responsibility; the auditor attests whether management has adhered to the Shari'a supervisory board's fatwas, rulings and guidelines (para 9).
Management must provide the auditor with all fatwas, rulings and guidelines issued by its Shari'a supervisory board and other relevant documents, e.g., Shari'a supervisory board reports (para 10).
The auditor makes specific inquiries of management, obtains representation letters about oral representations, and expects management to provide complete, accurate, and timely information (para 11).

Audit scope references ASIFIs and applicable national standards; International Standards on Auditing and national standards apply to matters not covered by ASIFIs provided they do not contravene Shari'a Rules and Principles; due to test nature and inherent limitations of audits and internal control systems, there is an unavoidable risk that some material misstatement may remain undetected (para 12).

Engagement letter shall refer to the form of reports/communications beyond statutory reports to equity holders (e.g., a report to management on internal control weaknesses), state the auditor's need for unrestricted access to records and information, and note the expectation of written management representations (paras 13-14).
Engagement letter should state the basis on which fees are computed and billing arrangements (para 15).
Engagement letter should request the client to confirm the terms of engagement by acknowledging receipt (para 16).

Other matters that may be included: audit planning arrangements, description of other letters/reports, arrangements for consultation with the client's Shari'a supervisory board, involvement of other auditors/experts, arrangements with a predecessor auditor, restrictions of auditor liability, and further arrangements (para 17).

For audits of a component (subsidiary, branch, or division) of a parent Islamic financial institution, factors influencing whether to send a separate engagement letter include who appoints the component's auditor, whether a separate report is issued, legal requirements, extent of other auditors' work, degree of parent ownership, and degree of independence of component management (para 18).

On recurring audits, the auditor considers whether circumstances require revising the terms of engagement or reminding the client of existing terms; a new letter may be warranted where the client misunderstands the objective/scope, terms are revised, there is a recent change of senior management/equity holders/board/ownership, a significant change in the client's business, or legal requirements (paras 19-20).

A request to change the engagement to one providing a lower level of assurance requires the auditor to consider the appropriateness of doing so; a change due to changed circumstances or a misunderstanding of the nature of the service is ordinarily reasonable, but not if it relates to incorrect, incomplete, or unsatisfactory information provided by the client (paras 21-23).

Before agreeing to change an audit engagement to a related service (e.g., a review), the auditor considers legal or contractual implications; if there is reasonable justification and the audit work complies with ASIFIs for the changed terms, the report issued should not reference the original engagement or procedures performed under it, except where changed to an agreed-upon procedures engagement (paras 24-25).

Where terms of engagement are changed, the auditor and client should agree on the new terms; the auditor should not agree to a change lacking reasonable justification, such as changing to a review engagement to avoid a qualified opinion or disclaimer due to insufficient audit evidence regarding receivables (paras 26-27).

If the auditor cannot agree to a change of terms and is not permitted to continue the original engagement, the auditor should withdraw and consider any obligation, contractual or otherwise, to report the circumstances of withdrawal to other parties such as the board of directors or equity holders (para 28).

Standard is effective for financial statements for financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1419 A.H. or 1 January 1999 A.D., and was adopted by the Accounting and Auditing Standards Board at meeting No. (13), held 10-11 Safar 1418 A.H., corresponding to 15-16 June 1997 A.D. (Effective Date; Adoption of the Standard).

standards.title: Testing for Compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles by an External Auditor (Auditing Standard No. (4))
standards.effective_date: 2002-01-01, for financial statements for financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1423 A.H. or 1 January 2002 A.D. (para 18)
standards.applicability: Applies to the external auditor of an Islamic financial institution (IFI) testing for compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles in connection with the audit of the IFI's financial statements (para 1); the term “auditor” refers only to the external auditor and does not apply to any internal audit function of the IFI (para 2).
term_names: Auditing Standard for Islamic Financial Institutions (ASIFI)
Governance Standard for Islamic Financial Institutions (GSIFI)
standards.structure: Introduction (paras 1-4); Responsibility of an External Auditor for Compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles (paras 5-8); Scope of the Auditor’s Work (paras 9-15); Reference to the SSB’s Report in the Auditor’s Report (para 16); Making the Auditor’s Draft Report Available to the SSB (para 17); Effective Date (para 18); Adoption of the Standard (unnumbered, adoption note).
key_points: Purpose of this ASIFI is to establish standards and provide guidance on testing for compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles by an external auditor, in connection with the audit of financial statements of an IFI conducting business in conformity with Shari’a Rules and Principles (para 1).
The term “auditor” in this ASIFI refers only to the external auditor and does not apply to any internal audit function associated with the IFI (para 2).
The auditor shall obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide reasonable assurance that the IFI has complied with Shari’a Rules and Principles (para 3).

Per ASIFI (1), “reasonable assurance” is the concept relating to accumulation of audit evidence necessary for the auditor to conclude there are no material misstatements in the financial statements taken as a whole, and relates to the whole audit process (para 3).

Per ASIFI (1), reasonable assurance also means the auditor has satisfied himself that the transactions examined during the audit comply with Shari’a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB of the financial institution (para 3).
The term “institution/institutions” is used to represent Islamic financial institutions, including banks (fn 1).
The steps set out in the standard support the requirements of this ASIFI (para 4).

The auditor is responsible for forming and expressing an opinion on the financial statements; IFI management is responsible for ensuring the financial statements and the IFI’s activities comply with Shari’a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB, per ASIFI (1) and ASIFI (2) (para 5).
Per Governance Standard for Islamic Financial Institutions (GSIFI) No. (1), the responsibility to interpret Shari’a Rules and Principles lies with the SSB (para 6).

The auditor shall be knowledgeable about Shari’a Rules and Principles but would not possess the same level of knowledge as SSB members, and shall not be expected to provide interpretation of these rules and principles (para 7).

The fatwas, rulings and guidance issued by the SSB form the basis on which the auditor considers whether the IFI has complied with Shari’a Rules and Principles, and the auditor uses these as a basis for concluding whether financial statements were prepared in accordance with Shari’a Rules and Principles (para 8).
The auditor's responsibility is to form an opinion on whether the IFI's transactions comply with the fatwas, rulings and guidance issued by the IFI's SSB (para 9).
The auditor shall have no responsibility for assessing the competence of members of the SSB (para 10).

The auditor shall satisfy himself that the IFI's process for introducing new products or modifying existing products includes appropriate procedures for ensuring compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles, including reviews by IFI management, internal audit and the SSB (paras 11).
The auditor shall include procedures to ensure that all new fatwas, rulings and guidance, and modifications to existing ones, are identified and reviewed for each period under examination (para 12).

The auditor shall review available documents to ensure all product types offered by the IFI have been reviewed by the SSB per GSIFI No. (2), including SSB reports on Shari’a compliance and SSB minutes of meetings, and give consideration to their effect on the auditor's work (para 13).

The auditor shall also verify, on a test basis, that transactions entered into by the IFI are consistent with the fatwas, rulings and guidelines of the SSB; the nature and extent of testing is subject to the IFI's individual circumstances and determined by the auditor (para 14).

The auditor shall review the findings of internal reviews carried out by IFI management, internal audit, and the internal Shari’a review set out in GSIFI No. (3), and consider whether these findings affect the nature, timing or extent of the auditor's work (para 15).
The auditor shall make the auditor's report available only after taking note of the SSB's draft report on the IFI's compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles (para 16).

If the SSB's draft report indicates that compliance with Shari’a Rules and Principles is lacking and the auditor decides, based on that draft report, to modify his draft report, he shall provide an adequate explanation of the nature of and reasons for the modification (para 16).
Prior to issuance of the SSB's final report, the auditor shall make available to the SSB his draft report and conclusions related to Shari’a compliance (para 17).
This Standard shall be effective for financial statements for financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1423 A.H. or 1 January 2002 A.D. (para 18).
The standard was adopted by the Accounting and Auditing Standards Board in its meeting No. (19), held on 17 Safar 1421 A.H., corresponding to 21 May 2000 A.D. (Adoption of the Standard).

standards.title: Auditor’s Responsibility to Consider Fraud and Error in an Audit of Financial Statements
standards.effective_date: financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1425 A.H. / 1 January 2004 A.D. (para 21)
linked_standards: ASIFI No. (1), Objective and Principles of Auditing
AAOIFI Code of Ethics for Employees of Islamic Financial Institution
standards.applicability: Applies to auditors of Islamic financial institutions (IFIs), including Islamic banks and Islamic insurance companies, in relation to funds of investment accountholders (IAH) and policyholders (PA) (paras 1, 5a); to be read in conjunction with all ASIFIs issued by AAOIFI and complements IFAC standards with IFI-specific requirements (para 3); no exclusions stated (absent).
term_names: Auditing Standard for Islamic Financial Institutions (ASIFI)
standards.structure: Introduction (paras 1-3); Definition and Cases of Error (para 4); Definition and Cases of Fraud (para 5); Responsibility of an Auditor (paras 6-7); Professional Skepticism (paras 8-9); Consideration of Fraud, Error and Audit Procedures (paras 10-12); Considering the Effect of an Auditor's Report (para 13); Documentation (paras 14-16); Responsibility of Management and Corporate Governance Body (paras 17-19); Management Representations (para 20); Effective Date (para 21); Adoption of the Standard (unnumbered, p.880)
key_points: Standard establishes guidance on the auditor's responsibility to consider the risk of fraud and error in an audit of an IFI's financial statements; primary responsibility for prevention/detection rests with those charged with corporate governance and management of the IFI (para 1).
Auditor shall consider the risk of material misstatements resulting from fraud and error when planning, performing, and evaluating audit procedures (para 1).

Standard provides guidance on characteristics of fraud/error and limits of auditor responsibility, minimum procedures for indications/inquiries/discussions of fraud and error, and guidance on management representations regarding fraud and error (para 2 a-c).
Standard is read in conjunction with all ASIFIs issued by AAOIFI and complements IFAC standards on fraud and error by adding IFI-specific requirements (para 3).

Error defined as unintentional misstatement including omission of an amount or disclosure: incorrect accounting estimate under Financial Accounting Standards from oversight/misunderstanding of facts; mistake applying AAOIFI accounting principles/standards; incorrect application or oversight of Shari'a rules and principles (para 4 a-c).
Fraud defined as an intentional act by management, those charged with governance, employees, or third parties, involving deception to obtain an unjust or illegal advantage (para 5).

Fraud cases specific to IFIs include breach of contracts with investors/third parties such as misappropriation of funds of IAH (Islamic banks) or PA (Islamic insurance companies), and intentional misallocation of profits between the IFI and IAH/PA (para 5 a-b).

Fraud cases include the IFI's misuse of IAH and PA funds including violation of contracts, and intentional non-disclosure by management of activities/information to the Shari'a supervisory board, auditors, investors and shareholders (para 5 c-d).

Fraud cases include intentional, consistent violation/misinterpretation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings and guidelines, and intentional manipulation of documents/records to misrepresent the IFI's financial statements (para 5 e-f).

Audit objective, per ASIFI No.(1), is to opine whether financial statements are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with Shari'a rules and principles, AAOIFI accounting standards, and relevant national standards/regulations (para 6).
The auditor is not and cannot be held responsible for prevention of fraud and error, though the audit may act as a deterrent (para 6).

Auditor held responsible for negligence/misconduct if reasonable efforts were not made to design/plan the audit to detect fraud and error, or if aware of material fraud/error and did not report it to the appropriate authority (para 7).

Auditor applies professional skepticism per ASIFI No.(1) para 6; must evaluate management's compliance with AAOIFI Shari'a standards and Shari'a supervisory board fatwas/rulings, and the SSB report alone shall not be the sole basis for the auditor's compliance conclusion (para 8).
Absent contrary evidence, auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine and is not expected to be a document-authentication expert (para 9).

In planning the audit, auditor shall assess the risk that fraud and error may cause material misstatement to the financial statements and to the assets, balances and income of the IAH/PA funds (para 10).

Inquiries must include discussions with Shari'a supervisory board members on compliance judgement/interpretation, extent of Shari'a review coverage, controls over IAH/PA asset management, and effectiveness of internal control systems safeguarding IAH/PA assets, income and balances (para 11).
Auditor shall inquire whether management, audit committee, or Shari'a supervisory board members are aware of any fraud and error suspected, discovered, investigated and/or reported (para 12).

Where financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud/error, auditor considers audit implications and whether to continue with a qualified opinion or possible disclaimer per ASIFI No.(3), paragraphs (27-46) (para 13).

Auditor must document fraud and error risk factors identified during assessment and the auditor's response, including any additional procedures triggered, plus discussions held with Shari'a supervisory board members supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas/rulings (paras 14-16).

Management/governance body is responsible for prevention and detection of fraud and error, must maintain a culture of honesty compatible with the AAOIFI Code of Ethics for Employees of Islamic Financial Institutions, and set controls for Shari'a rules and principles compliance; auditor shall assess that management developed an appropriate internal control system including Shari'a compliance (paras 17-19).

Auditor shall obtain written management representations covering: compliance with AAOIFI Shari'a standards/SSB fatwas; disclosure of fraud/error matters; compliance with IAH/PA contract provisions; presentation of all SSB fatwas/rulings to auditors; and controls placed over IAH/PA assets, income and balances (para 20 a-e).
Effective date: financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1425 A.H., corresponding to 1 January 2004 A.D. (para 21).
Standard adopted by the Accounting and Auditing Standards Board at meeting No.(25) in Bahrain on 3 Rabi' I 1424 A.H., corresponding to 3 May 2003 A.D. (Adoption of the Standard).

key_points: External Shari'ah audit is defined as an independent assurance engagement to provide reasonable assurance that an IFI complies with 'Shari'ah principles and rules' applicable to its financial arrangements, contracts and transactions during a specific period (para 8c).

Two engagement types are recognized: a direct external Shari'ah audit (preferred by the standard) and an attestation external Shari'ah audit, used where required by a jurisdiction's regulators and a management statement of compliance is required (para 5).

Direct engagement objective: obtain reasonable assurance, based on suitable criteria (para 15), that the IFI has in all material respects complied with Shari'ah principles and rules for a specific audit period, and report accordingly (para 6).

Attestation engagement objective: obtain reasonable assurance whether the management's statement of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules presents fairly the state of compliance, in all material respects, and report accordingly (para 7).

This ASIFI must be read in conjunction with ISAE 3000; ISAE 3000 requirements apply to such engagements unless contrary to or inconsistent with a requirement of this standard, or a requirement of Shari'ah (paras 2-3).

Criteria hierarchy for assessing Shari'ah compliance (para 15): (a) AAOIFI Shari'ah standards; (b) the regulator's regulations insofar as they entail regulatory Shari'ah requirements; (c) rulings of the Central Shari'ah Board; (d) AAOIFI Financial Accounting Standards insofar as Shari'ah-related; (e) approvals/rulings of the IFI's own Shari'ah Supervisory Board; in case of ambiguity, the SSB's clarification prevails (para 15 explanation).

IFIs are defined to include banking, insurance/Takaful, capital markets and similar activities, and expressly include stand-alone branches, divisions and windows of conventional financial institutions offering Shari'ah-compliant products and services (para 8g).

The external Shari'ah auditor is defined as a firm with professional auditing knowledge and Shari'ah competence meeting the regulator's/Central Shari'ah Board's fit-and-proper criteria; the (financial) external auditor may also be appointed as the external Shari'ah auditor (para 8d).
Ethical requirements: the auditor shall comply with AAOIFI's "Code of Ethics for Accountants and Auditors of Islamic Financial Institutions" as well as other applicable codes of ethics (para 10).
Quality control: in addition to ISQC 1, the auditor must have adequate resources and knowledge of the criteria, entailing active involvement of Shari'ah expert(s) throughout the engagement (para 11).

Materiality must be assessed both quantitatively (tolerable amount, observed deviation rate) and qualitatively (nature, cause and severity of an observation from the Shari'ah perspective); tolerance limits may differ from a financial statements audit (paras 21-22).

Sampling: determination of need and sample size is based on principal risk assessment (inherent, control, and combined risk for testing of details) and materiality; sample sizes shall be increased where instances of Shari'ah non-compliance are identified (paras 24-25).

Written representations must emphasize adequacy of internal control/governance for Shari'ah compliance, completeness of information provided, and disclosure of any known Shari'ah non-compliance; if the IFI refuses to provide requested representations, the auditor shall disclaim his opinion (paras 26-30).

The auditor may use the work of the internal Shari'ah review/audit function and the Shari'ah supervisor(s)' report(s) if independent of management and reliable; the Shari'ah compliance department/function (a management function) cannot be used as a partial replacement for the external Shari'ah auditor's work (paras 31-33).

Residual risk not adequately addressed by procedures performed shall be assessed and reduced via testing of details, including analytical and detailed verification, e.g. recomputation of profit-and-loss distribution to investment account holders (para 34).

The external Shari'ah auditor's report must include: title, addressee (shareholders of the IFI unless otherwise required by the regulator), identification of subject matter/criteria/subject matter information, management's responsibility statement, statement on compliance with this standard and ISAE 3000, ethical/quality-control statement, procedures summary, statement on involvement of Shari'ah experts, opinion in positive form, report date (no earlier than the date sufficient evidence was obtained, including the SSB's report), auditor's name/firm/location, and a statement that a long form report is being issued (para 38).

A long form report (LFR) is issued alongside the short form report, addressed to those charged with governance (not shareholders or the public), covering key audit matters/observations including those resolved via adjustment, charity or reversal (para 40; Appendix C).

Modified opinions (qualified, adverse, or disclaimer) are required where there is material non-compliance, the subject matter information omits material information, or the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence; the report must clearly describe the reasons for modification (paras 41-42).
Detailed application guidance is to be issued separately as an "External Shari'ah Audit Manual" (para 43).
Effective date: this standard is effective for external Shari'ah auditors' reports covering periods beginning on or after 01 January 2020; early adoption is encouraged (para 44).

The original effective date of 01 January 2019 was deferred to 01 January 2020 via the AGEB statement on COVID-19 impact (issued 4 Dhul-Qa'dah 1441H / 25 June 2020); engagements already initiated under the original requirements, or where required by the regulator, remain valid under the standard (fn 3, citing paras 33-35 of the AGEB statement).

The standard was presented for approval and unanimously approved (no reservations) at the AAOIFI Governance and Ethics Board's 6th meeting, held 18-19 Rabi' I 1439H, corresponding to 6-7 December 2017 (Appendix D).

The standard is classified as an auditing standard (not a governance standard), applying primarily to external Shari'ah auditors rather than IFIs directly, and remains non-mandatory until the auditing standards revision project is concluded (BC3-BC5).

The Basis for Conclusions (Appendix E) was approved at the Board's 20th meeting, 15-16 Sha'ban 1442H, corresponding to 29-30 March 2021; the updated standard with Basis for Conclusions appended was issued on 23 Ramadan 1442H, corresponding to 5 May 2021 (Appendix F, H13).
divergence_notes: "The board discussed about the risk of difference of opinion between the external Shari'ah auditor and the SSB. Another scenario is different interpretations of a Shari'ah standard or the requirements of a regulator or a central Shari'ah board... it was decided to include an explanation to the hierarchy that in case of a difference of opinion, the interpretation by the SSB shall prevail" (BC26).

"there is diversity in regulators' approaches around the world" regarding whether to require a direct or attestation-type external Shari'ah audit, which is why the standard retains both engagement types (BC13).
